lines: בִּטְחוּ, הוּא יַעֲנֶה, בִּטְחוּ, הוּא יַעֲנֶה
כִּי תָמִיד אַתָּה לָנוּ עֵזֶר טוֹב
אֵין דּוֹמֶה לוֹ, מוֹשִׁיעַ רַךְ וְקָרוֹב

review: 1:1–2 is the refrain printed alone as the first stanza, the same shape as tr0218/0219; the Arabic doubles ثِقُوا هُوَ يُجِيبُ inside one line and the Hebrew keeps the doubling, then adds the object of the answer (תְּפִלַּת קְדוֹשָׁיו) as the Arabic's دُعَاءَ الْقِدِّيسِين does.

2:4 וְשׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה — the Arabic وَسَامِعُ الصَّلَاةِ is the psalm title (Ps 65:3, שֹׁמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה); the participle is kept as a title of God rather than turned into a clause, so the line names what He is, not what He does.

3:2 בִּמְלֶאכֶת הַצְּלָב — the Arabic بِعَمَلِ الصَّلِيب is 'by the work of the cross'; מְלָאכָה is kept for עֲבֹדָה/עמל-work, so the cross is a deed done and not merely an event, which is what makes the rhetorical question of 3:3 work.

3:3–4 הֲיִפָּלֵא … מַשְׁקִיט מַיִם — the Arabic's two clauses are Job 42:2 (לֹא־יִבָּצֵר מִמְּךָ מְזִמָּה) and Ps 107:29 (יָקֵם סְעָרָה לִדְמָמָה); the sea is stilled בְּצִוּיוֹ, which keeps the word of command rather than a general 'by His order'.

4:3 נִפְגְּשֵׁהוּ בֶעָנָן — the Arabic نَلْقَاهُ فِي السَّحَاب is 1 Thess 4:17 (נִפָּגֵשׁ … בֶּעָנָנִים); the Hebrew keeps the meeting verb and the cloud, so the stanza ends on the same event the epistle names.
